_comment: Curated content for the interactive launch-readiness tool. The item SET, grouping, step-by-step guides and env vars live here; each item's `match` is the register ref (in docs/launch-readiness.md) whose status drives whether it shows as complete. Run tools/launch-readiness/generate.mjs to rebuild docs/launch-readiness.html; a hook does this automatically when the register changes.

sections.title: Infrastructure & accounts
sections.note: The critical path. Hosting first — it unblocks KMS, storage, email and the deploy. Everything here replaces a dev stub with a real service; the app reads a real key as an env change, never a code change.

items.title: Choose hosting, then provision Postgres, Redis, TLS & domain
items.when: First — before any live-mode or partner review
items.why: The one decision the rest of the list waits on.
steps: Shortlist a host that gives you managed Postgres with point-in-time recovery (PITR) and managed Redis in an EU/UK region (your consumers are UK) — Fly.io, Render, or AWS are the candidates in the plan.
Note the constraint: a partner security review may dictate the choice, so don't over-commit spend before that conversation.
Create the account and provision the database (turn PITR on), Redis, and a domain with TLS.
Put the connection strings and domain into the production environment. Redis is a cache only — never a source of truth (the app already assumes this).

items.title: AWS KMS master key (envelope encryption)
items.why: Encrypts the signing keys, link tokens and webhook secrets. Replaces the fake-kms dev container.
steps: In AWS KMS, create a symmetric key for envelope encryption.
Create an IAM role/user scoped to kms:Encrypt, kms:Decrypt, kms:GenerateDataKey on that key only.
Set MERITED_KMS_ENDPOINT, MERITED_KMS_KEY_ID and the AWS credentials in prod.
Roadmap note for the auditor (LEAD-5): native Ed25519 KMS is the ratified upgrade path — fine to launch on the current envelope scheme.

items.title: S3 bucket for published head-hashes
items.why: The external audit anchor — third parties fetch daily head-hashes to verify the ledger grew append-only.
steps: Create an S3 bucket for heads/* with public read on the head objects (or front it with a CDN).
This is deliberately public — the whole point is that anyone can fetch a head-hash and check it. No secrets live here.
Set MERITED_HEADS_BUCKET (and MERITED_HEADS_ENDPOINT only if you use MinIO).
Then run test A3: S3ObjectStore put/get/list + verify-chain --against-heads s3://….

items.title: Resend account + verified sending domain
items.why: Sends magic links and hosted-linking codes. Dev uses Mailpit.
steps: Create a Resend account and add your sending domain.
Add the SPF, DKIM and DMARC DNS records Resend gives you, and wait for verification — this is what keeps magic links out of spam.
Create an API key; set MERITED_RESEND_API_KEY and MERITED_RESEND_FROM.
Then run test A6: confirm magic links and linking codes land in real inboxes.

items.title: Generate & pin production VAPID push keys
items.why: Identity for Web Push. Self-generated — no vendor.
steps: Generate a keypair — the standard tool is one command:
Set the three env vars. MERITED_VAPID_SUBJECT is a contact (mailto: or an https: URL).
Pin them — regenerating invalidates every existing push subscription. Dev uses throwaway keys.

items.title: Observability sink (traces + alerts)
items.why: OTel traces plus the alerts that catch a merchant quietly dropping conversions, or a head-publication failure.
steps: Create an Axiom or Grafana Cloud account and get an OTLP endpoint + token.
Point the OTel exporter env vars at it (dev uses console/memory exporters).
Wire two alerts: mint_vs_claim_under_reporting and head-publication failure.

sections.title: Payments & compliance
sections.note: These have external review clocks measured in weeks, and two of them gate real money. Start them in parallel with the infrastructure above, not after.

items.title: Stripe Connect platform account
items.why: Pays out agent commissions. Platform review takes weeks. Build already runs on SimulatedPayouts.
steps: Create a Stripe account and apply to enable Connect as a platform.
Complete the KYB / platform questionnaire — this is the slow part, so submit it now.
Use Express connected accounts (recommended in the plan).
In test mode, grab the secret key + webhook signing secret; set MERITED_STRIPE_SECRET_KEY and MERITED_STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET.
The env-loader deliberately refuses live keys until the lawyer (LEAD-2) and auditor (LEAD-5) sign off — expected.
Then run test A7: a real test-mode transfer end-to-end, with the transfer ID captured as evidence.

items.title: Payments lawyer — PSR / EMI perimeter
items.why: Determines whether the money-flow makes you a payment institution / e-money issuer, and how to structure to avoid it.
steps: Engage a UK payments/fintech lawyer on the PSR/EMI question.
Get a clear read on the perimeter and the required structure for commission payouts.
File the outcome in docs/decisions/ — it unlocks live-mode in the env-loader.

items.title: External security audit
items.why: Independent review (2–5 days). This is the SYN-32 substitute — the crypto stayed library-only pending it.
steps: Book an external security auditor for a 2–5 day review.
Give them the recent internal hardening pass (16 workstreams, docs/hardening-log.md) and the Phase-1 hardening pack as context — but this is the independent look, not a repeat of it.
Track every finding to closure before any real-money or production exposure.

items.title: Trademark screen for the “Valet” name
items.when: Before the recorded demo circulates / investor materials
items.why: A quick clearance so the name is safe to put in front of investors.
steps: Run a UK IPO (and USPTO if relevant) screen on the Valet product name.
Clear it before the Act-2 recording or any investor deck goes out.

sections.title: Commerce integrations
sections.note: Needed for the Shopify and loyalty-partner rails. The code is done and green against simulators — this is the real-store / real-partner wiring.

items.title: Shopify Partner account, dev store & app review
items.when: App review runs concurrently — start with Phase 2
items.why: The Grade-A Shopify rail. Code is ready (PH3-5 ✅) against a simulated store.
steps: Create a Shopify Partner account and a development store.
Register the app and request protected-customer-data access (the review runs in the background).
Grab the app API key/secret.

For test A12: point the store's orders/paid webhook at /v1/merchants/:slug/shopify/orders-paid, register the app secret as that merchant's webhook secret, and have the theme/checkout extension write the merited_token cart attribute.

items.title: Partner IdP registration (real loyalty programme)
items.when: When a real programme partner exists
items.why: Account linking beyond the FakeAurora stand-in.
steps: When you sign a real loyalty programme, register its OIDC client (id/secret) per programme into the IdP registry.
FakeAurora keeps standing in until then — no rush without a partner.

sections.title: Engineering follow-ups
sections.meta: hand to Claude Code / an engineer
sections.note: Small, well-scoped code tasks left over from the build and hardening. None block each other; several just wait on hosting existing.

items.title: Bump drizzle-orm + nodemailer, then raise the CI audit gate
items.when: Whenever — it's a version bump + retest
items.why: Two fixable HIGH advisories: a drizzle-orm SQL-identifier injection and a nodemailer file-read/SSRF. The CI audit gate currently blocks on critical only.
steps: Bump drizzle-orm to ≥ 0.45.2 and nodemailer to ≥ 9.0.1 (plus the 8 moderate / 1 low), then re-run the full suite.
Raise the CI dependency-audit gate from --audit-level=critical to --audit-level=high.
Fastest path: ask Claude Code — “bump drizzle-orm and nodemailer to clear the audit HIGHs, re-run build/test/lint, and raise the CI audit gate to high.”

items.title: Enable GitHub code scanning (surface CodeQL results)
items.when: Before CI is a launch gate
items.why: The CodeQL SAST job is wired but runs advisory — its results only appear once code scanning is on.
steps: In the repo: Settings → Code security → Code scanning, and enable it (needs GitHub Advanced Security for a private repo).
Once uploads land, drop continue-on-error: true from the codeql job so it becomes a real gate.

items.title: Edge HSTS / CSP at the load balancer
items.why: The app already emits HSTS in prod as defence-in-depth; the edge should own it, plus any org-wide CSP.
steps: At the TLS-terminating edge/CDN, set Strict-Transport-Security (the app uses max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains, no preload).
Decide on preload enrolment — it's irreversible, so treat it as a deliberate step.
Confirm the Secure session cookie actually rides HTTPS end-to-end (NODE_ENV=production, MERITED_ENV unset), and add any org-wide CSP.

items.title: Runtime DNS-rebinding guard for Web Push
items.when: Before real Web Push goes live
items.why: The SSRF guard is a static check — it can't see a hostname that resolves to a private IP at send time.
steps: Add a runtime resolve-then-check-IP guard (or an egress allowlist / proxy) so a rebinding push endpoint can't reach an internal host via the VAPID POST.
Engineering task — pair it with the real-push work (test A5).

items.title: Merchant-facing proof-pack export endpoint / CLI
items.why: Today the proof-pack builder lives in the verifier test harness — fine for the gate, not a merchant feature.
steps: Build a production endpoint/CLI that assembles a merited-proof-pack/1 for a given claim, so a merchant or auditor can export and verify offline.

items.title: Wire the send-on-quote push trigger in production
items.why: A production caller of PushService.sendQuoteNotification was left as an open seam in Phase 1.
steps: Wire the production trigger that fires the approval push when a quote is minted for a consumer with a live subscription.

items.title: Settle the control-plane e2e flake under parallel load
items.why: Next boot + TOTP window occasionally flakes the control-plane e2e when the whole suite runs in parallel.
steps: Confirm CI runner sizing or serialise the control-plane e2e suites so a green run is trustworthy on the first try.

sections.title: Real-world tests
sections.meta: once the infra above is up
sections.note: CI proves the code; these prove the real vendors deliver. Each unlocks as its service (section 01/02/03) comes online.

items.title: Real-S3 head-publication smoke test
items.why: put/get/list + verify-chain against the live heads bucket.

items.title: Postgres PITR restore drill
items.why: Restore into a scratch instance and run verify-chain on the copy — proves backups actually recover.

items.title: Real email deliverability (Resend)
items.why: Magic links + linking codes land in real inboxes with SPF/DKIM/DMARC passing.

items.title: Stripe test-mode transfer, end-to-end
items.why: A real transfer ID in the evidence — the Phase-2 gate clause.

items.title: Web Push against a real browser push service
items.why: CI proves the encrypted request; this proves FCM/Mozilla actually deliver it.

items.title: Valet LLM interpreter, flag OFF (real Anthropic API)
items.why: Natural-language briefs parse, or fail closed to the scripted path.

items.title: Load / rate-limit under production-shaped traffic
items.why: Per-agent + per-merchant limits, Redis limiter, replay-cache hit rates under real load.

items.title: Wallet UI cross-browser + accessibility sweep
items.why: Push-permission prompts differ per browser; confirms the W13–W15 a11y work holds live.

items.title: Shopify dev-store end-to-end
items.why: Install → cart-attribute token → orders/paid → verified claim.

items.title: Timed key-rotation operational drill
items.why: Routine < 15 min, compromise < 60 min, minuted for the auditor.

items.title: Record the demo (Act 1 human-mode + Act 2)
items.why: The demo assets — Act 2 recorded with VALET_DETERMINISTIC=1.
